questions.q: A solar eclipse coincided with the death of the Prophet’s infant son, and people began to link the two. What did the Prophet tell them?
options: That they should make noise to end it
Not quite. The article says: Eclipses are not caused by anyone’s death; they are signs of God, and a time for prayer and charity.
That the eclipse was indeed a sign of mourning
Not quite. The article says: Eclipses are not caused by anyone’s death; they are signs of God, and a time for prayer and charity.
Eclipses are not caused by anyone’s death; they are signs of God, and a time for prayer and charity
Yes. He corrected the belief though it seemed to honour his family.
That such things should not be discussed
Not quite. The article says: Eclipses are not caused by anyone’s death; they are signs of God, and a time for prayer and charity.
questions.rationale: “Eclipses of the sun and moon are not due to the death of any human being; they are just two signs given by God.”

questions.q: How, according to the article, did separating the Creator from the creation open the way to science?
options: People lost interest in nature
Not quite. The article says: Nature was no longer held sacred and feared, so it could be explored and put to use.
Old books of myths were translated
Not quite. The article says: Nature was no longer held sacred and feared, so it could be explored and put to use.
Scholars were paid to study the stars
Not quite. The article says: Nature was no longer held sacred and feared, so it could be explored and put to use.
Nature was no longer held sacred and feared, so it could be explored and put to use
Well reasoned. Awe gave way to enquiry.
questions.rationale: “The awe surrounding nature was replaced with a spirit of research and enquiry… the phenomena of nature, looked upon by ancient man with reverence, have now become objects of investigation.”

questions.q: For whom, the article says, is the careful ritual of burial really meant?
options: The living – so that they see their own end in the dead and take a lesson
Right. They “experience death before death arrives.”
The family’s standing in society
Not quite. The article says: The living – so that they see their own end in the dead and take a lesson.
The dead person alone
Not quite. The article says: The living – so that they see their own end in the dead and take a lesson.
Those who dig the graves
Not quite. The article says: The living – so that they see their own end in the dead and take a lesson.
questions.rationale: “Its significance is for those who are still alive. Through a dead person an important lesson is conveyed to living people—that they, too, will meet the very same fate one day.”

questions.q: A petal and a feather are easily spoiled by a touch. What does the article say is more delicate still?
options: The human heart – to wound it is a grave wrong in God’s eyes
Yes. And onlookers who do nothing share the blame.
A spider’s web
Not quite. The article says: The human heart – to wound it is a grave wrong in God’s eyes.
A child’s toy
Not quite. The article says: The human heart – to wound it is a grave wrong in God’s eyes.
A drop of dew
Not quite. The article says: The human heart – to wound it is a grave wrong in God’s eyes.
questions.rationale: “There is something even more fragile and delicate than a petal or a feather, and that is, the human heart.”

questions.article: The Power and Price of Peace
questions.q: Everything has a price. What does the article say is the price of peace?
options: Great wealth
Not quite. The article says: Willingness to tolerate loss.
Willingness to tolerate loss
Correct. Refusing to bear loss leads easily to violence.
A strong army
Not quite. The article says: Willingness to tolerate loss.
Silence on every matter
Not quite. The article says: Willingness to tolerate loss.
questions.rationale: “What is the price of peace? It is to tolerate loss.”

questions.article: The Power and Price of Peace
questions.q: Why does the article say that patiently accepting a loss is not defeat?
options: It keeps one balanced and able to rebuild with what remains – “after every evening a new morning dawns”
Well read. It takes courage, not weakness.
Because losses are never real
Not quite. The article says: It keeps one balanced and able to rebuild with what remains – “after every evening a new morning dawns”.
Because no one else will come to know of it
Not quite. The article says: It keeps one balanced and able to rebuild with what remains – “after every evening a new morning dawns”.
Because the loss is later repaid by others
Not quite. The article says: It keeps one balanced and able to rebuild with what remains – “after every evening a new morning dawns”.
questions.rationale: “To patiently accept and tolerate loss is not tantamount to defeat. Rather, it is something that requires great courage and boldness… one still has many resources left, on the basis of which one can rebuild one’s life.”

questions.q: A believer may err in a fit of emotion. What does the article say he does once the passion cools?
options: Explains why he was justified
Not quite. The article says: Feels ashamed, seeks out the person he wronged, asks forgiveness and makes amends.
Waits for the other person to forget
Not quite. The article says: Feels ashamed, seeks out the person he wronged, asks forgiveness and makes amends.
Feels ashamed, seeks out the person he wronged, asks forgiveness and makes amends
Yes. He errs, but does not stoop to baseness.
Breaks off relations to avoid embarrassment
Not quite. The article says: Feels ashamed, seeks out the person he wronged, asks forgiveness and makes amends.
questions.rationale: “When the passion cools, one becomes conscious of the error and feels ashamed… The next step is to seek out the wronged person, beg forgiveness and make amends.”

questions.q: The mind is compared to a mirror that reflects reality exactly. Why, then, do people fail to accept a truth placed before them?
options: Truth is always hidden
Not quite. The article says: Something comes in between – an attachment, self-interest or pride.
The mind is too weak to grasp truth
Not quite. The article says: Something comes in between – an attachment, self-interest or pride.
They have not studied enough
Not quite. The article says: Something comes in between – an attachment, self-interest or pride.
Something comes in between – an attachment, self-interest or pride
Exactly. Like an object placed between a mirror and what it should reflect.
questions.rationale: “It is always personal attachments and commitments that prevent one from accepting truth.”

questions.q: Why, in the article’s view, do holidays and outings fail to remove stress?
options: Travel is tiring
Not quite. The article says: Modern stress is intellectual in nature, and physical remedies cannot solve it.
Holidays are too short
Not quite. The article says: Modern stress is intellectual in nature, and physical remedies cannot solve it.
People take work with them
Not quite. The article says: Modern stress is intellectual in nature, and physical remedies cannot solve it.
Modern stress is intellectual in nature, and physical remedies cannot solve it
Right. It needs a higher level of thinking – the remembrance of God.
questions.rationale: “The real problem is that modern day stress is intellectual in nature, while people are trying physical means to de-stress themselves.”

questions.q: The verses speak of the earth and heavens being formed in stages. What does the commentary infer from creation by stages?
options: That it is planned – and a plan points to an all-knowing Planner
Well reasoned. Order implies purpose.
That the universe made itself slowly
Not quite. The article says: That it is planned – and a plan points to an all-knowing Planner.
That the earth is older than the heavens
Not quite. The article says: That it is planned – and a plan points to an all-knowing Planner.
That creation was left unfinished
Not quite. The article says: That it is planned – and a plan points to an all-knowing Planner.
questions.rationale: “Creation in this way—in other words by stages, means planned creation; and… it essentially follows that it has a Planner who has purposefully created it according to a set plan.”
